title: bonsai.status/1
description: bonsai status --json (contract §12): one workspace at a glance, for the studio's bridge and an assistant (Bonsai has no screens of its own: every visual is the studio's). Printed, never stored. Written by bonsai status --json (cheap and offline; --full adds checks); read by the studio's bridge and agents. Spec §16 row 24's additions arrive as values, not new fields: a pack not installed on this machine is a needs entry of kind plugin, the Claude Code floor a needs entry of kind tool (never a problem, warn only), plugin drift and a bonsai on the PATH that is not the installed one are problems; --line prints the statusline's workspace half instead of this document. A writer writes every field below, in this order (contract §2.2); when Bonsai cannot read the workspace at all it exits 3 and fills format, bonsai, problems and error, with every other field null. Absolute paths appear only here, printed locally, and the bridge never forwards them (contract §2.6). A reader treats a missing field as null, keeps an unknown one and refuses a duplicate key.

format.description: The version, always the first field (contract §2.2).

bonsai.description: The version of the Bonsai that wrote this (contract §2.2).

mode.description: How the status was gathered: offline for the default (cheap, no network, no Claude Code) or full for --full (which asks the network and Claude Code); a reader shows a word it does not know as other, so the field is typed open (formats/README.md). null on exit 3.

workspace.description: The workspace: its id and name from bonsai.yaml, and the main checkout's absolute path (printed locally; the bridge keeps it in its registration and never forwards it). null on exit 3.

id.description: The workspace id: ws- and 26 lowercase base32 characters (contract §3).

root.description: The main checkout's absolute path, forward slashes.

home.description: The Bonsai home (BONSAI_HOME, else the user's .bonsai folder) and this workspace's machine folder in it (contract §3). null on exit 3.

path.description: The home's absolute path, forward slashes.

key.description: The machine folder's name under workspaces/: r- and the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the main checkout's real path.

local.description: The main checkout's record folders, absolute (under workspace.root), so the forwarder never builds paths; printed locally, never forwarded. null on exit 3.

formats.description: Which majors this Bonsai reads and writes, per format name (contract §2.2); the bridge reads a workspace only at majors it knows. It lists every format that has a major, so bonsai.error, which is part of other documents and has none, is not in it. null on exit 3.

read.description: The majors read (0 is format 0, today's files).

documents.description: Every document kind the workspace declares, Bonsai's and its packs' (contract §7.3). Each entry holds the §7.3 fields that apply: kind, from, path or file, id, format, statuses, person, agent, stamp, task_field. Only kind and from are required: §7.3 leaves which of the others are always written open (formats/README.md). null on exit 3.

from.description: Who declared it: bonsai or a pack id.

path.description: The folder holding one file per document (top level only), project-relative with forward slashes; absent or null for a kind that is one file.

file.description: The single file, project-relative; absent or null for a kind that is a folder.

id.description: The id pattern a document's id must match; an id resolves to exactly one file, never a path.

format.description: Its bonsai.* format, for Bonsai's kinds; absent or null for a pack's.

statuses.description: Its statuses, if any; the first is where a new document starts.

person.description: The status moves a person makes, as [from, to] pairs (contract §10.2).

agent.description: The status moves agents make, as [from, to] pairs.

stamp.description: Fields set to the day's date when a document reaches a status ({status: field}).

task_field.description: The field naming the task a document belongs to (a plan's task:).

packs.description: The packs, from the lock (contract §14), and whether this checkout's files match. null on exit 3.

version.description: The pack's version, from its tag.

state.description: ok, changed (a file the pack wrote was edited) or missing (contract §12).

files.description: Counts of edited and missing files the lock lists, and of changed format-0 files (contract §2.3). null on exit 3.

changed.description: Files the lock lists whose bytes were edited.

missing.description: Files the lock lists that are gone.

format0_changed.description: Format-0 files whose bytes no longer match the lock's format0 hash.

labels.description: The label namespaces in force, where each came from and its version (contract §5). null on exit 3.

from.description: Where its definitions came from: bonsai, a pack id, or machine (attached on this machine, contract §5.3).

lanes.description: The lanes defined in the workspace, with their rules (contract §6); [] when no pack defines lanes. null on exit 3.

close.description: The lane's close rule: person or agent.

status_writes.description: agents (agents move statuses themselves) or command (a managed workspace: moves go through status_command), from this machine's settings (contract §3, §10.1). null on exit 3.

status_command.description: The command a managed workspace's guard names for a status move; null when status_writes is agents.

person_only.description: The globs only a person may grant (contract §5.5), from bonsai.yaml; [] when none. null on exit 3.

active_task.description: The active task for this checkout and environment (contract §13): its id, how it was found (named or running, null when none), and why there is none. null on exit 3.

examples.why: no active task: two tasks read running (T-0901, T-0902)

id.description: The active task's id, or null when there is none.

how.description: named (given by --task or BONSAI_TASK), running (the single task reading running), or null when there is none.

why.description: Why there is none, one sentence, said first in every refusal it causes; null when there is one.
examples: no active task: two tasks read running (T-0901, T-0902)

needs.description: What the workspace needs from a machine, one entry per need (contract §12): kind, then id, name, source and version, each null where it does not apply. A pack (kind pack, or plugin for a pack not installed on this machine, spec §5) is named by id, with its source and version; a tool (the Claude Code floor among them, spec §7) by name, with the version it needs. A writer writes all five fields (contract §2.2). null on exit 3.

kind.description: What is needed, an open list (contract §12): pack, tool, mcp, shell; plugin for a pack not installed on this machine (spec §5).

id.description: For a pack or a plugin: the pack's id. null for other kinds.

name.description: For a tool: its name, such as claude-code for the Claude Code floor. null where it does not apply (a pack, a plugin).

source.description: For a pack or a plugin: where it is fetched from (a git URL). null for other kinds.

version.description: The version needed: a pack's version, or a tool's version range such as the Claude Code floor; null when none applies.

problems.description: One sentence each: the same findings bonsai check reports (a changed workspace id, plugin drift, a bonsai on the PATH that is not the installed one among them); [] when none. Never null: on exit 3 it says why the workspace could not be read. A stale generated table and an old Claude Code are warnings, never problems.
examples: bonsai.yaml's id changed from ws-7kq2m4xw5r3t6y2u7p4a5c3e2b to ws-3c5e7g2k4m6p2r4t6v3x5z7b2d

checks.description: With --full only: {packs, plugins, claude_code, mcp}: newer pack versions, this machine's plugins against the lock, Claude Code's version against the floor, and the MCP servers (a list, [] until step 5.5 fills it); null without --full. Its inner layout is not fixed, so it is typed open (formats/README.md).

error.description: null unless the command refuses or fails: on exit 3 (Bonsai cannot read the workspace at all) it says what went wrong and the next step, as bonsai.error has it (spec §3, §16 row 29).

examples.message: bonsai.yaml is not in this checkout, so it is not linked to Bonsai

next.do: run: bonsai init in the project's main checkout

code.description: What went wrong, as a fixed word: an open list (contract §2.2). Later steps add words, which is an addition (format review 4.5), and a reader shows a word it does not know as other. The known words live in one table in Bonsai's code, their one home, which bonsai check --schema bonsai.error prints (and, from step 5.1.10, the reference page of lists, docs/reference/lists.md); this schema does not copy them, and the words in its examples are illustrative.

message.description: What is wrong, one sentence for a person, in ASCII (spec §3).
examples: no --yes, and no terminal to ask at: nothing was written

next.description: The next thing to do (spec §3: every refusal and error names it, in the human line and in the JSON): what to do and who does it.

do.description: What to do: the command to run, written run: and the command line, or the step in plain words.
examples: open Claude Code in this checkout and accept its trust question

who.description: Who does it, a closed list: agent (any agent may do it, unattended) or person (a person's step: a consent such as --allow-exec, a tap, a setting, an install, or a command an agent's task does not grant it; spec §4, §6).
